sources.title: Cornelia Drutu and Michael Kapovich, Geometric Group Theory, revised 837-page manuscript
sources.locator: Targeted complete passages: §7.10.2 Definitions 7.98–7.99, canonical enlargement and Lemma 7.101; §9.7.4 Definitions 9.101–9.102 and Propositions 9.103–9.104; Lemma 10.25; §10.4 ultralimit construction and Lemmas 10.48, 10.51; §10.6 opening unnumbered cone definition (PDF p.372) and Remark 10.67; §11.20 Proposition 11.167/Lemma 11.168; §11.21 Definition 11.175/Proposition 11.176/Lemma 11.177; Theorem 11.181. Locators below delimit the harvested text; this is not a claim to have read all of Chapters 7–11.

contents.name: Bounded real ultralimits and free ultrafilters
contents.locator: §10.1, Lemma 10.25 (complete proof); filter definitions and cofinite example preceding it
contents.support: Use the compact-interval specialization, proved locally by deterministic bisection. Free-tail extension uses the exact published AC-based ultrafilter theorem. Reject Remark 10.1: induction does not prove countable choice in ZF. Local prerequisite supplement in the owned strategy proves the rational reciprocal Cauchy estimate with a nonstrict first comparison, and maximality of the null ideal, from the six named earlier deps; this supplement is local mathematics, not a claim about the monograph text.

contents.name: Pointed ultralimit quotient and asymptotic cone
contents.locator: §10.4 initial sequence-space construction; §10.6 opening unnumbered cone definition (PDF p.372)
contents.support: Multiply distances by lambda_n→0; preserve arbitrary basepoint sequences and a fixed free ultrafilter. Restrict to uniformly rescaled-bounded representatives; exceptional coordinates are replaced by basepoints.

contents.name: Ultradistance and quotient equivalence
contents.support: Supply all equivalence, representative-independence and triangle-inequality details locally from bounded real calculus.

contents.name: Geodesic limits and limits of isometries
contents.locator: §10.4 Lemma 10.48, Exercise 10.49, Definition 10.50 and Lemma 10.51 (complete target proofs)
contents.support: Separate original endpoints alpha_n,beta_n from scaled a_n=lambda_n alpha_n,b_n=lambda_n beta_n. Evaluate gamma_n(clamp(t,-a_n,b_n)/lambda_n); the scaled distance identity and projection inequality prove isometry and represented-point surjectivity, including escaping endpoints. Explicit AC selects original geodesics and origin witnesses.

contents.name: Oriented rays, complete geodesics, and their parameter domains
contents.locator: §1.2, p.45 (a geodesic is an isometric embedding of an interval); §10.4 Lemmas 10.48–10.51, PDF pp.365–366; §11.18 discussion of biinfinite geodesics, p.391
contents.support: Supports the interval-domain convention. The local definition additionally fixes origins, signed parameters, tails and common-tail terminology; the owned ultralimit lemma treats the three possible domains without a compact nearest-point choice.

contents.name: Minsize and perimeter-bounded minsize function
contents.support: Use chosen geodesic sides, allow degeneracies, and prove attainment locally. Define slimness and trees locally without later HG items.

contents.name: Uniform two-side bound from tree cones
contents.support: Negate the ratio bound and rescale at a point realizing Hausdorff distance. Separate two segments, rays, and lines; finite Hausdorff distance contradicts the earlier local tree rules.

contents.name: All-cones converse through full fat-triangle extraction
contents.locator: §11.20 Proposition 11.167(a), complete proof following Lemma 11.168, PDF pp.443–445
contents.support: Preserve bounded/unbounded third-side distance ratios and global maximality over every triangle side. Replace ideal-boundary shorthand by signed segment parameters and common-tail rules.

contents.name: Fixed scales n^{-1} with all nonprincipal ultrafilters
contents.reason: The binding interface quantifies all ordinary null scales for one fixed free ultrafilter. This alternate quantifier formulation is not needed by any owned proof or consumer; no reindexing assertion is imported.

contents.name: Every cone segment is a limit segment under sublinear minsize
contents.support: Retain the equality forcing x=c, then parameter-surjectivity for the whole segment. Add the bounded-perimeter case explicitly.

contents.name: Sublinear minsize criterion
contents.locator: §11.21 Proposition 11.176, reverse direction and complete Lemma 11.177 proof, PDF pp.448–449
contents.support: All chosen cone segments are limits, hence minsize zero makes cone triangles tripods; use the locally proved converse.

contents.name: Hyperbolicity implies bounded minsize
contents.reason: The source imports its earlier centroid estimate. The owned criterion needs the reverse direction; the forward thin-triangle-to-centroid interface belongs to the later quantitative hyperbolic toolkit and is not used here.

contents.name: Coarse triangle and filling conventions
contents.support: Explicit finite triangulated disk and vertex map; area counts even degenerate image triangles. No global coarse simple-connectivity theorem is assumed when a disk is supplied.

contents.name: Singular diagrams from normal-closure expressions
contents.locator: §7.10.2 Definitions 7.98–7.99 and Lemma 7.101, complete proof, PDF pp.261–265
contents.support: Local finite polygonal disk/collar lemma and explicit triangular-collapse map replace the invalid identity extension. Temporary midpoint subdivisions reduce loop occurrences to simple-arc folds; enclosed-lobe deletion and literal spur insertion preserve the stated invariants. E<=Lm+n. Proposed repair awaits final adjudication.

contents.name: Canonical enlargement of a diskoid to a disk
contents.locator: §7.10.2 paragraph defining canonical enlargement after Definition 7.98; Exercise 7.100
contents.support: Local disk/collar lemma supplies topology. Compatible vertex disks, bands and face caps use 4d, 8 and 4k triangles respectively. Total 16E+4I+4<=20(L+1)(m+n+1), with explicit boundary repetitions and bounded edge labels. Proposed repair awaits final adjudication.

contents.name: Algebraic area and coarse disk construction
contents.locator: §7.10.2 Lemma 7.101 and canonical enlargement; §9.7.4 bounded-edge fillings
contents.support: Use at most Area(w) relator faces and count E<=L Area(w)+|w| before the owned thickening. The local construction exports C(L)(Area(w)+|w|+1) and proves the unit-edge realization metric and endpoint rounding inline.

contents.name: Algebraic area equals minimum diagram area in both directions
contents.reason: The exact-area interface is already scoped to the singular-disc toolkit and published-consumer repair. HG-P needs only the controlled existence direction and does not invoke the exercise as a proved theorem.

contents.name: Planar distance-coordinate coverage mechanism
contents.locator: §9.7.4 Proposition 9.103, complete proof; Proposition 9.104, complete proof
contents.support: Replace the source assertion of separation by an explicit signed-crossing proof on finite polygonal maps. Area subadditivity is finite polygon dissection, not measure theory.

contents.name: Square-root area bound for minsize
contents.support: Correct the vertex-to-affine-edge step by h=m/2-r. This yields m<=2r sqrt(N)+2r and a further 2e boundary-approximation term. The sharper displayed constant in the source is not used.

contents.name: Subquadratic filling route, specialized to linear relator area
contents.locator: §11.22.1 Theorem 11.181 and its complete proof, PDF p.452
contents.support: Minsize squared is controlled by coarse area; linear algebraic area yields a common square-root majorant with constants tracked in K,L. AC propagates from the cone criterion.

contents.name: General subquadratic coarse filling theorem
contents.reason: The broader metric filling interface needs a definition of the global coarse isoperimetric function. This supplier pair exports the required finite-presentation specialization and the square-root inequality; the general formulation is not assumed.

contents.name: Point-wedge contradiction for uniformity
contents.support: Local extension, not a quoted theorem: define the wedge metric and classify triangles by their vertex factors. The actual root segments in a two-factor triangle form a core triangle of no greater perimeter.

contents.name: Uniformity for common filling data
contents.locator: Proposition 11.176 with the point-wedge construction modeled by Example 11.9
contents.support: Local inference: if no common slimness bound exists, wedge countably many violating spaces with the same sublinear majorant. The local wedge lemma and sublinear criterion contradict the unbounded selected slimness. This argument supplies a dependence only on K,L, not an explicit formula.

contents.name: Cone of the real line
contents.support: For the line compute the isometry by lim lambda_n(x_n-e_n). Tree cones use the owned zero-minsize and segment lemmas with AC.

contents.name: Euclidean scaling obstruction
contents.support: Local explicit right-triangle computation gives s/2<=minsize<=s and perimeter (2+sqrt(2))s. Dilation establishes exact proportionality; no optimal coefficient is claimed.

contents.name: Rescaled bounded and unbounded perimeter cases
contents.support: Compute lambda_n m(P_n)<=epsilon lambda_n P_n+lambda_n P0, and independently compute a Euclidean triangle at scale n. The B items do not supply one another.

sources.title: Frigerio and Sisto, Characterizing hyperbolic spaces and real trees
sources.locator: §1.1 (entire subsection, PDF p.1); §1.3 Definition 3 and complete sequence quotient construction (PDF pp.2–3); §3 Lemma 11 and complete proof (PDF pp.7–8).

contents.name: Rips slimness and zero-hyperbolic real trees
contents.support: Independent treatment of chosen geodesics and 0-slimness. Local unique-arc equivalence is supplied separately.

contents.name: Asymptotic cone definition
contents.support: Source divides by d_n→infinity, equivalent to local lambda_n=1/d_n. Arbitrary observation points are preserved.

contents.name: Unique arcs and tree segments
contents.locator: §3 Lemma 11, entire statement and proof, PDF pp.7–8
contents.support: The path-containment proof supplies the topological content missing from simply calling a 0-slim space a tree. Local branch classes and elementary interval extrema fill in this proof route without global topology imports. The path-separation step is supplemented inline by a complete least-upper-bound argument on [0,1], avoiding a later connectedness supplier.

sources.title: Martin R. Bridson, The geometry of the word problem
sources.locator: §4.1 Singular Disc Diagrams and Proposition 4.1.2, complete proof; §4.2 Definition 4.2.1, Theorem 4.2.2, Lemma 4.2.3 with Figure 4.2.4 and Remark 4.2.5, Lemma 4.2.6 and final proof of Van Kampen’s Lemma. PDF pp.20–24.

contents.name: Singular planar labelled diagrams, outer walks and exterior fold/spur moves
contents.locator: §4.1, especially the singular-disc conventions and Proposition 4.1.2; §4.2 Definition 4.2.1, Lemma 4.2.3, Remark 4.2.5 and Lemma 4.2.6, PDF pp.20–24
contents.support: Supplies the finite plane-diagram and outer-walk conventions. The owned definition records loops, thin edges, cut vertices and vertex labels explicitly; the local lemma supplies the PL fold/deletion and incidence proof.

contents.name: Area-nonincreasing boundary reduction and reinsertion
contents.support: Local finite polygonal disk/collar lemma and explicit triangular-collapse map replace the invalid identity extension. Temporary midpoint subdivisions reduce loop occurrences to simple-arc folds; enclosed-lobe deletion and literal spur insertion preserve the stated invariants. E<=Lm+n. Proposed repair awaits final adjudication.

contents.name: Controlled diagram existence from lollipops
contents.support: Provides the direction Area(diagram)<=algebraic area without bounding conjugators. Combine the local surviving-edge count and regular-neighbourhood thickening; the source alone does not export the desired triangle count.

contents.name: Area equality and diagram-to-product implication
contents.reason: Keep the exact-area consumer repair on its existing Phase-2 supplier pair. The owned coarse filling uses only the other direction; no defective published disk theorem is imported.

contents.name: Conjugator length bounded by diagram diameter
contents.reason: The coarse triangle estimate is controlled by relator perimeter and face/boundary incidence, not conjugator lengths or diagram diameter. This extra bound has no use in the assigned proof route.

sources.title: Jeff Erickson, Simple Polygons
sources.locator: Sections 1.2 and 1.4, PDF pp.4-9, and Section 1.6 Theorem 1.10, PDF pp.13-14: polygon separation, triangulation and finite PL disk parametrization. Complete relevant arguments read. Prescribed-boundary fan extensions and positive-width collars are local constructions, not quoted source claims.

contents.name: Finite polygon separation and triangulation supporting disk/collar surgery
contents.locator: Sections 1.2, 1.4 and 1.6, Lemma 1.4 and Theorems 1.5 and 1.10
contents.support: Use the finite triangulation-to-convex-polygon PL map of Theorem 1.10. Extend a prescribed PL boundary map by matched center fans on the two convex polygons, then compose using finite triangle refinements. Normalize the fold on two genuine embedded polygonal disks produced by a positive-width notch. No annulus-cut disk model or ambient-plane extension is consumed. No recorded Jordan theorem or later plane-graph item is a supplier; the quantitative count remains local.

sources.title: Jeff Erickson, Planar Graphs (2023)
sources.locator: Abstract graphs, Planar graphs and planar maps, Rotation systems: complete relevant sections read. Only dart/germ, occupied-side and boundary-successor conventions are used; the generic Jordan appeal and graph algorithms are not imported.

contents.name: Distinct loop germs and edge-side successor walks
contents.support: Define the local cyclic germ successor explicitly and use it to verify bigon deletion: the interior germ block is removed, exterior successors bypass precisely the cancelled pair, and retained characteristic face walks are unchanged. Polygon separation and the relative peeling homotopy are proved locally, not assumed from this source.
